To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found a way to optimize the on-board processing to fit the allowed bandwidth, while minimizing the signal distortion, and that this method has been validated by the ground tests.
the on-board processing is able to achieve the required data rate with an acceptable level of distortion.

(i) a method to optimize the Planck/LFI data handling chain has been developed and successfully applied; (ii) the on-board processing has been optimized and the required data rate achieved; and (iii) the processing noise has been kept below the 10% level of the instrumental white-noise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of an automated tool for tuning Planck/LFI's on-board data compression.
a set of problems that are relevant for the Planck/LFI mission.
the optimization of the on-board data handling system of the Planck/Low Frequency Instrument based on minimal loss of information in the downstream processing chain downstream of the processing unit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Planck/LFI instrument is ready to fly, the on-board processing has been successfully tested and tuned, and that the required compression level and the required processing noise have been achieved.
the on-board data handling is working as expected and the data quality is fully compliant with the science objectives.
the LFI on-board data handling chain has been optimized in flight and is performing as planned.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of the on-board processing has been optimized to provide a better estimation of the effective noise temperature, which in turn is a key parameter for the science pipeline.
the on-board processing has been successfully tuned to meet the requirements and the performance of the Planck/LFI instrument has been successfully verified against the requirements.
we have developed an automated procedure for tuning on-board data processing to cope with the data rate constraints of the spacecraft and the data volume allocated to LFI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LFI on-board processing chain, tuned to fit the allowed bandwidth, is able to preserve the information in the data to a level well above the required level.
, despite the lossy nature of the compression, the LFI on-board processing allows to recover virtually all the relevant scientific information and to achieve very close to the required data rate.
the on-board data handling chain can be tuned to cope with the required data rate while keeping to a level compatible to the science objectives the distortion introduced by the lossy compression.
